title: Oklahoma's Biggest Comeback: 25 Points at Baylor, 2019
question: What is the largest comeback in Oklahoma football history?
answer: On November 16, 2019, No. 10 Oklahoma rallied from a 28-3 deficit to beat No. 13 Baylor 34-31 in Waco. Coverage of the game called the 25-point comeback the largest in Oklahoma history.
summary: On Nov. 16, 2019, No. 10 Oklahoma erased a 28-3 deficit to beat No. 13 Baylor 34-31 in Waco, a 25-point rally reported as the biggest in OU history.
body: On this date in 2019, Oklahoma climbed out of one of the deepest holes in program history. The No. 10 Sooners traveled to Waco to face No. 13 Baylor, which was riding an 11-game winning streak, and early in the second quarter they trailed 28-3.

Baylor led 31-10 at halftime, and the game looked gone. Instead, Oklahoma shut the Bears out in the second half and scored 24 unanswered points, which news coverage at the time described as the largest comeback in OU history.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts, in his lone season as a Sooner, led the charge. He finished 30 of 42 for 297 yards and four touchdown passes, all of them after the 28-3 mark, and ran for 114 yards. He also had three turnovers, so the rally came despite some rough moments of his own.
Hurts threw a two-yard touchdown pass to Brayden Willis with 5:25 left to tie the game at 31. Kicker Gabe Brkic then hit a 31-yard field goal with 1:45 remaining to put Oklahoma ahead 34-31.

Baylor drove to the Oklahoma 40 on its final possession, but linebacker Nik Bonitto intercepted the pass with 29 seconds left to seal it. The loss ended Baylor's winning streak and badly hurt its playoff hopes, while Oklahoma stayed in the Big 12 title race.
